articles.title: Coefficient of a divisor at a point
articles.statement:
For a divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$ and a
point $P \in C$, the coefficient of $D$ at $P$ is the integer $D(P)$.

articles.title: Divisors on a curve
articles.statement:
For a set $C$ (the points of a curve), a divisor on $C$ is a finitely
supported function $D \colon C \to \mathbb{Z}$. Its support is the finite set of points
$P \in C$ with $D(P) \neq 0$.

articles.title: Coefficients of the pole part
articles.statement:
For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$ and every
point $P \in C$, the coefficient at $P$ of the pole part $D^-$ of $D$ is $\max(-D(P), 0)$.

articles.title: The pole part of a divisor is effective
articles.statement:
For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$,
the pole part $D^-$ of $D$ is effective: $D^-(P) \ge 0$ for every point $P \in C$.

articles.title: Pole part of a divisor
articles.statement:
For a divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$, the pole part $D^-$ of
$D$ is the divisor on $C$ whose coefficient at each point $P \in C$ is $\max(-D(P), 0)$.

articles.title: Coefficients of the zero part
articles.statement:
For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$ and every
point $P \in C$, the coefficient at $P$ of the zero part $D^+$ of $D$ is $\max(D(P), 0)$.

articles.title: The zero part of a divisor is effective
articles.statement:
For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$,
the zero part $D^+$ of $D$ is effective: $D^+(P) \ge 0$ for every point $P \in C$.

articles.title: A divisor is its zero part minus its pole part
articles.statement:
For every set of points $C$ and every
divisor $D$ on $C$, let $D^+$ be its zero part, with coefficient $\max(D(P), 0)$ at each point
$P$, and $D^-$ its pole part, with coefficient $\max(-D(P), 0)$ at each point $P$. Then
$D^+ - D^- = D$.

articles.title: Zero part of a divisor
articles.statement:
For a divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$, the zero part $D^+$ of
$D$ is the divisor on $C$ whose coefficient at each point $P \in C$ is $\max(D(P), 0)$.

articles.title: Evaluation is multiplicative
articles.statement:
For a commutative group $G$, every function
$f : C \to G$ and all divisors $D_1, D_2$ on $C$, writing $f(D)$ for the evaluation of a
divisor $D$ against $f$, we have $f(D_1 + D_2) = f(D_1) \, f(D_2)$.

articles.title: Evaluation is a product over the support
articles.statement:
For a commutative group $G$, every function
$f : C \to G$ and every divisor $D$ on $C$, the evaluation of $D$ against $f$ equals
$\prod_{P \in \operatorname{supp} D} f(P)^{D(P)}$, the product over the points in the support
of $D$.

articles.title: Evaluation of divisors as a group homomorphism
articles.statement:
For a commutative group $G$ and a
function $f : C \to G$, this is the monoid homomorphism from the group of divisors on $C$,
written multiplicatively, to $G$ that sends a divisor $D$ to the finite product
$\prod_{P \in \operatorname{supp} D} f(P)^{D(P)}$.

articles.title: Evaluation of a one-point divisor
articles.statement:
For a commutative group $G$, every function
$f : C \to G$, every point $P \in C$ and every integer $n$, the divisor $n \cdot P$, with
coefficient $n$ at $P$ and $0$ elsewhere, evaluates against $f$ to $f(P)^n$.

articles.title: The zero divisor evaluates to one
articles.statement:
For a commutative group $G$ and every function
$f : C \to G$, the evaluation of the zero divisor on $C$ against $f$ is the identity element
$1$ of $G$.

articles.title: Evaluation of an integer multiple
articles.statement:
For a commutative group $G$, every function
$f : C \to G$, every integer $n$ and every divisor $D$ on $C$, writing $f(D)$ for the
evaluation of $D$ against $f$, we have $f(nD) = f(D)^n$.

articles.title: Evaluation of a divisor against a function
articles.statement:
For a commutative group $G$, a function
$f : C \to G$ and a divisor $D$ on $C$, the evaluation of $D$ against $f$ is the element
$f(D) = \prod_{P \in \operatorname{supp} D} f(P)^{D(P)}$ of $G$.

articles.title: Degree of a holomorphic map
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is,
compact connected Hausdorff spaces with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$. Every
holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$ has a degree, which is a natural number.

The intended value is $0$ when $f$ is constant and the usual degree of $f$ otherwise.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: A compact Riemann surface has genus zero iff it is a sphere
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact
Riemann surface, that is, a compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas
modelled on $\mathbb{C}$. The genus of $X$ is $0$ if and only if $X$ is homeomorphic to the unit
sphere in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Genus of a compact Riemann surface
articles.statement:
For a compact Riemann surface $X$, that is, a compact
connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$, the genus of $X$
is a natural number.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Jacobian of a compact Riemann surface
articles.statement:
For a compact Riemann surface $X$, that is, a
compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$, the
Jacobian $J(X)$ of $X$ is a type in the same universe as $X$.

Separate wanted instances make $J(X)$ a compact Hausdorff commutative complex Lie group modelled
on $\mathbb{C}^g$, where $g$ is the genus of $X$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Abel–Jacobi map is holomorphic
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$,
and let $J(X)$ be its Jacobian, a complex manifold modelled on $\mathbb{C}^g$. For every point
$P \in X$, the Abel–Jacobi map $X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ is holomorphic.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Abel–Jacobi map is injective in positive genus
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface
with Jacobian $J(X)$, and let $P \in X$. If the genus of $X$ is positive, then the Abel–Jacobi map
$X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ is injective.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Abel–Jacobi map sends the base point to zero
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface
with Jacobian $J(X)$, an abelian group. For every point $P \in X$, the Abel–Jacobi map
$X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ sends $P$ to $0$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Abel–Jacobi map
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface with Jacobian $J(X)$. Each point
$P \in X$ gives a map $X \to J(X)$, the Abel–Jacobi map based at $P$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Pullback on Jacobians is compatible with composition
articles.statement:
Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be compact
Riemann surfaces, and for a holomorphic map $h$ between compact Riemann surfaces write $h^*$ for
the induced pullback map on Jacobians. For all holomorphic maps $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$
and every point $P$ of the Jacobian $J(Z)$, we have $(g \circ f)^*(P) = f^*(g^*(P))$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The pullback map on Jacobians is holomorphic
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces
of genus $g_X$ and $g_Y$, with Jacobians $J(X)$ and $J(Y)$, complex manifolds modelled on
$\mathbb{C}^{g_X}$ and $\mathbb{C}^{g_Y}$. For every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the induced
pullback map $f^* : J(Y) \to J(X)$ is holomorphic.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Pullback along the identity
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact,
connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifold of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for its
Jacobian. For every $P \in J(X)$, the pullback of $P$ along the identity map of $X$ is $P$:
$(\mathrm{id}_X)^*(P) = P$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Pullback on Jacobians
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact,
connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for the
Jacobian of $X$, an abelian group with a topology. For a holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the
pullback $f^*$ is a continuous group homomorphism from $J(Y)$ to $J(X)$. It is meant to be the
zero map when $f$ is constant and the usual pullback along $f$ otherwise; its properties are
stated separately.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Pushforward respects composition
articles.statement:
Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that
is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$
for the Jacobian of $X$. For all holomorphic maps $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ and every
$P \in J(X)$, the pushforwards satisfy $(g \circ f)_*(P) = g_*(f_*(P))$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The pushforward on Jacobians is holomorphic
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces,
that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, of genera
$g_X$ and $g_Y$. The Jacobian $J(X)$ of $X$ is a complex-analytic manifold modeled on
$\mathbb{C}^{g_X}$, and likewise $J(Y)$ on $\mathbb{C}^{g_Y}$. For every holomorphic map
$f : X \to Y$, the pushforward $f_* : J(X) \to J(Y)$ is holomorphic.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Pushforward along the identity
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact,
connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifold of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for its
Jacobian. For every $P \in J(X)$, the pushforward of $P$ along the identity map of $X$ is $P$:
$(\mathrm{id}_X)_*(P) = P$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Pushforward of a pullback is multiplication by the degree
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact
Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension
one, and write $J(Y)$ for the Jacobian of $Y$, an abelian group. For every holomorphic map
$f : X \to Y$ and every $P \in J(Y)$, the pushforward along $f$ of the pullback of $P$ along $f$
is $\deg(f) \cdot P$, where the degree $\deg(f)$ is a natural number:
$f_*(f^*(P)) = \deg(f) \cdot P$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Pushforward on Jacobians
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact,
connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for the
Jacobian of $X$, an abelian group with a topology. For a holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the
pushforward $f_*$ is a continuous group homomorphism from $J(X)$ to $J(Y)$. It is meant to be
the homomorphism induced by $f$; its properties are stated separately.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge. Problem `jacobian_challenge_diffgeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The uniform Mordell–Lang constant is at least one
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $g$ and
$d$, the uniform constant satisfies $c(g, d) \ge 1$.

articles.title: Uniform Mordell–Lang constant
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $g$ and $d$, $c(g, d)$ is a natural
number: the constant in the uniform bound on rational points of curves in Theorem 1.1 of
Dimitrov, Gao and Habegger.

## Sources

- V. Dimitrov, Z. Gao, and P. Habegger, `Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves`, Annals of Math, 194 (1) 2021. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_uniform_mordell_lang` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Abel–Jacobi map sends the base point to zero
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be a proper, smooth,
geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$, let $J(C)$ be its Jacobian, and let $P$ be a
$k$-rational point of $C$. The Abel–Jacobi map $C \to J(C)$ based at $P$ sends $P$ to the
identity point of $J(C)$ for its group scheme structure.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge/near/587802685. Problem `jacobian_challenge_alggeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Universal property of the Jacobian
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible
curve over a field $k$, let $J(C)$ be its Jacobian, let $P$ be a $k$-rational point of $C$, and
let $\iota_P : C \to J(C)$ be the Abel–Jacobi map based at $P$. Let $A$ be a group scheme over $k$
that is smooth, proper and geometrically irreducible. For every morphism of $k$-schemes
$f : C \to A$ sending $P$ to the identity point of $A$, there is a unique morphism of $k$-schemes
$g : J(C) \to A$ with $f = g \circ \iota_P$.

In other words, the Jacobian of $C$ is the Albanese variety of $C$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge/near/587802685. Problem `jacobian_challenge_alggeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Genus of a smooth proper curve
articles.statement:
For a field $k$ and a curve $C$ over $k$, that is, a
$k$-scheme that is proper, smooth of relative dimension $1$ and geometrically irreducible, the
genus of $C$ is a natural number.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge/near/587802685. Problem `jacobian_challenge_alggeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Group law on the rational points of the Jacobian
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be a proper, smooth,
geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$. The commutative group structure on the set of
$k$-rational points of the Jacobian $J(C)$ is the one induced by its commutative group scheme
structure: the product of two $k$-points $x$ and $y$ is $\mu \circ (x, y)$, where $\mu$ is the
multiplication morphism of $J(C)$.

This pins down the group law rather than allowing an arbitrary commutative group structure.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge/near/587802685. Problem `jacobian_challenge_alggeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Jacobian of a smooth proper curve
articles.statement:
For a field $k$ and a curve $C$ over $k$, that is, a
$k$-scheme that is proper, smooth of relative dimension $1$ and geometrically irreducible, the
Jacobian $J(C)$ of $C$ is a $k$-scheme.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge/near/587802685. Problem `jacobian_challenge_alggeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Abel–Jacobi map
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field
$k$. Each $k$-rational point $P$ of $C$ gives a morphism of $k$-schemes $C \to J(C)$ from $C$ to
its Jacobian, the Abel–Jacobi map based at $P$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge/near/587802685. Problem `jacobian_challenge_alggeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Jacobian has dimension equal to the genus
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically
irreducible curve over a field $k$. The Jacobian $J(C)$ is smooth of relative dimension $g$ over
$k$, where $g$ is the genus of $C$.

## Sources

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian%20challenge/near/587802685. Problem `jacobian_challenge_alggeo` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Uniform Mordell–Lang for curves
articles.statement:
Let $g \ge 2$ and $d \ge 1$ be natural numbers, let $F$
be a number field with $[F : \mathbb{Q}] \le d$, and let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically
irreducible curve over $F$. If $C$ has genus $g$, then the number of $F$-rational points of $C$,
possibly infinite, is at most $c(g, d)^{1 + \rho}$, where $c$ is the uniform constant and $\rho$
is the free rank of the group of $F$-rational points of the Jacobian of $C$.

## Sources

- V. Dimitrov, Z. Gao, and P. Habegger, `Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves`, Annals of Math, 194 (1) 2021. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_uniform_mordell_lang` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Adele ring
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $K$ a field with $F$ a $K$-algebra. The adele ring
$\mathcal{A}_F$ of $F/K$ is the restricted product of copies of $F$ indexed by the places $P$
of $F/K$, with respect to their valuation rings $\mathcal{O}_P$ and the cofinite filter: its
elements are the families $\alpha = (\alpha_P)_P$ with $\alpha_P \in F$ for every place $P$
and $\alpha_P \in \mathcal{O}_P$ for all but finitely many $P$. See [Stichtenoth, Definition
1.5.2].

articles.title: Faltings' theorem (Mordell conjecture)
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $F$ a function
field over $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. If the genus
of $F/K$ is at least $2$, then $F/K$ has only finitely many places of degree one, that is,
places $P$ whose residue field (the quotient of the valuation ring of $P$ by its maximal ideal)
has dimension $1$ over $K$.

## Sources

-. Problem `faltings` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Finitely many poles
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a function field over a field $K$, that is, a finite
extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. For every $x \in F$, there are only finitely
many places $P$ of $F/K$ whose valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_P$ does not contain $x$, that is,
$x$ has only finitely many poles. See [Stichtenoth, Corollary 1.3.4].

## Sources

-. Problem `faltings` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Genus as the dimension of the adele class space
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a function field over a
field $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. The genus $g$ of
$F/K$ equals the dimension over $K$ of the quotient
$\mathcal{A}_F / (\mathcal{A}_F(0) + F)$, where $\mathcal{A}_F$ is the adele ring,
$\mathcal{A}_F(0)$ the integral adeles, and $F$ is embedded in $\mathcal{A}_F$ by the algebra
map of the $F$-algebra structure on the adeles (stated separately to be the principal
embedding). See [Stichtenoth, Corollary 1.5.5].

The dimension is the finite rank, taken to be $0$ if the quotient is infinite-dimensional.

## Sources

-. Problem `faltings` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Genus of a function field
articles.statement:
For a function field $F$ over a field $K$, that is, a finite
extension of the rational function field $K(t)$, the genus of $F/K$ is a natural number $g$,
specified by the separately stated formula $g = \dim_K \mathcal{A}_F / (\mathcal{A}_F(0) + F)$,
where $\mathcal{A}_F$ is the adele ring and $\mathcal{A}_F(0)$ the integral adeles.
See [Stichtenoth, Corollary 1.5.5].

## Sources

-. Problem `faltings` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The adele algebra map is the principal embedding
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a function field over a
field $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. The algebra map
$F \to \mathcal{A}_F$ of the $F$-algebra structure on the adele ring $\mathcal{A}_F$ equals the
principal adele map $F \to \mathcal{A}_F$.

## Sources

-. Problem `faltings` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Integral adeles
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $K$ a field with $F$ a $K$-algebra. The integral
adeles $\mathcal{A}_F(0)$ form the $K$-subspace of the adele ring $\mathcal{A}_F$ of $F/K$
consisting of the adeles $\alpha = (\alpha_P)_P$ whose coordinate $\alpha_P$ lies in the
valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_P$ of $P$ for every place $P$ of $F/K$. See [Stichtenoth,
Definition 1.5.3].

articles.title: Place
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $K$ a field with $F$ a $K$-algebra. A place of $F/K$ is a
valuation ring of $F$ containing $K$ and different from $F$: a $K$-subalgebra $\mathcal{O}$ of
$F$ with $\mathcal{O} \neq F$ such that $z \in \mathcal{O}$ or $z^{-1} \in \mathcal{O}$ for
every $z \in F$. See [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.4 and 1.1.8].

Stichtenoth calls the maximal ideal of $\mathcal{O}$ the place, which determines $\mathcal{O}$,
and also requires $\mathcal{O} \neq K$; that condition is omitted since it is automatic.

articles.title: Coordinates of a principal adele
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a function field over a field $K$, that is,
a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. For every $x \in F$ and every place
$P$ of $F/K$, the coordinate at $P$ of the principal adele of $x$ is $x$.

## Sources

-. Problem `faltings` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Principal adele map
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a function field over a field $K$, that is, a finite
extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. The principal adele map is a ring homomorphism
from $F$ to the adele ring $\mathcal{A}_F$ of $F/K$. It is meant to be the diagonal embedding
sending $x \in F$ to the adele whose coordinate at every place $P$ of $F/K$ is $x$, which is
well defined since $x$ has only finitely many poles; this coordinate formula is stated
separately.

## Sources

-. Problem `faltings` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Weil conjectures
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, and let $X$ be a scheme
over $\operatorname{Spec} F$ whose structure morphism is proper, geometrically irreducible and
smooth of relative dimension $d$. Then there is a sequence $A_0, A_1, A_2, \dots$ of finite
multisets of complex numbers with $A_0 = \{1\}$ such that, for every $0 \le i \le 2d$, the
multiset $A_{2d-i}$ is the image of $A_i$ under $\alpha \mapsto q^d/\alpha$, the multiset $A_i$
is invariant under every field automorphism of $\mathbb{C}$, and every $\alpha \in A_i$ is an
algebraic integer with $|\alpha| = \sqrt{q^i}$. Moreover, for every finite field extension $E$
of $F$ of degree $m$, the number of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec} E \to X$ over
$\operatorname{Spec} F$ equals $\sum_{i=0}^{2d} (-1)^i \sum_{\alpha \in A_i} \alpha^m$, where
the inner sums count multiplicities.

## Sources

- P. Deligne, 'La conjecture de Weil. I', Publications Mathématiques de l'Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques, Volume 43, pages 273–307 (1974), https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1974__43__273_0.pdf. See also references in the Lean file. Problem `weil_conjectures` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Galois elements as automorphisms of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ respect inverses
articles.statement:
For every
$\sigma$ in the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra
automorphism of the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ attached to $\sigma^{-1}$ is the
inverse of the automorphism attached to $\sigma$.

The equality holds by definition.

articles.title: Galois elements as automorphisms of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ respect products
articles.statement:
For all
$\sigma, \tau$ in the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the
$\mathbb{Q}$-algebra automorphism of the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ attached to
$\sigma\tau$ is the composite of the automorphisms attached to $\sigma$ and to $\tau$, with the
one attached to $\tau$ applied first.

The equality holds by definition.

articles.title: Galois elements as automorphisms of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$
articles.statement:
Each element $\sigma$ of
the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ is regarded as the
$\mathbb{Q}$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ of
$\mathbb{Q}$. Since $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is by definition the group of $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra
automorphisms of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, this map is the identity.

articles.title: Determinant character of the mod-$p$ Galois representation
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass
curve over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $p$ be a natural number, let $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be the group
of nonsingular points of $W$ with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$,
together with the point at infinity, and let $W[p]$ be its $p$-torsion subgroup, viewed as a
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-module. Let $\rho$ be the mod-$p$ Galois representation of the absolute
Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ on $W[p]$. Its determinant character is the group
homomorphism $G_{\mathbb{Q}} \to (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times$ sending $\sigma$ to the
determinant of the $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-linear automorphism $\rho(\sigma)$ of $W[p]$.

The determinant does not depend on a choice of basis, so no basis of $W[p]$ is fixed. The
definition is unconditional: if $W[p]$ has no finite basis over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, the
character is constantly $1$.

articles.title: Galois automorphisms as linear automorphisms of $W(p)$
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve
over $\mathbb{Q}$, $p$ a natural number, $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ the group of nonsingular
points of $W$ with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the
point at infinity, and $W[p]$ its $p$-torsion subgroup. For $\sigma$ in the absolute Galois group
$G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, this is the $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-linear map
$x \mapsto \sigma(x)$ on $W[p]$, where $\sigma$ acts on points through their coordinates, viewed
as a linear automorphism of $W[p]$ (the map is bijective).

articles.title: The linear Galois action on $W(p)$ is the action on points
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass
curve over $\mathbb{Q}$, $p$ a natural number, $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ the group of nonsingular
points of $W$ with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the
point at infinity, and $W[p]$ its $p$-torsion subgroup. For every $\sigma$ in the absolute Galois
group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ and every $x \in W[p]$, the image of $x$ under the
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-linear action of $\sigma$ on $W[p]$ is the point $\sigma(x)$ given by the
Galois action of $\sigma$ on all of $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$.

articles.title: Galois automorphisms act bijectively on $W(p)$
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over
$\mathbb{Q}$, $p$ a natural number, $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ the group of nonsingular points of
$W$ with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at
infinity, and $W[p]$ its $p$-torsion subgroup. For every $\sigma$ in the absolute Galois group
$G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-linear map by which $\sigma$ acts
on $W[p]$ is bijective.

The action of $\sigma^{-1}$ is a two-sided inverse.

articles.title: The linear Galois action on $W(p)$ respects products
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve
over $\mathbb{Q}$, $p$ a natural number, $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ the group of nonsingular
points of $W$ with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the
point at infinity, and $W[p]$ its $p$-torsion subgroup. For $\sigma$ in the absolute Galois group
$G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ and $x \in W[p]$, write $\sigma \cdot x$ for the image of $x$
under the $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-linear action of $\sigma$ on $W[p]$. Then for all
$\sigma, \tau \in G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ and every $x \in W[p]$,
$(\sigma\tau) \cdot x = \sigma \cdot (\tau \cdot x)$.

articles.title: The identity acts trivially on $W(p)$
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over $\mathbb{Q}$,
$p$ a natural number, $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ the group of nonsingular points of $W$ with
coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at
infinity, and $W[p]$ its $p$-torsion subgroup. Under the $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-linear action
of the absolute Galois group of $\mathbb{Q}$ on $W[p]$, the identity element maps every
$x \in W[p]$ to $x$.

articles.title: Linear Galois action on $W(p)$
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over $\mathbb{Q}$,
$p$ a natural number, $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ the group of nonsingular points of $W$ with
coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at
infinity, and $W[p]$ its $p$-torsion subgroup; it is a $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-module because
$p$ annihilates it. For $\sigma$ in the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$,
this is the $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-linear map $W[p] \to W[p]$, $x \mapsto \sigma(x)$, where
$\sigma$ acts on points through their coordinates.

articles.title: The Galois action on points is compatible with multiplication
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass
curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and let $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be the group of nonsingular points of
$W$ with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at
infinity. For $\sigma$ in the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ and
$P \in W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$, let $\sigma \cdot P$ be the point obtained by applying $\sigma$
to the coordinates of $P$ (the point at infinity is fixed). Then for all
$\sigma, \tau \in G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ and every $P \in W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$,
$(\sigma\tau) \cdot P = \sigma \cdot (\tau \cdot P)$.

articles.title: The identity acts trivially on points
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over $\mathbb{Q}$
and let $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be the group of nonsingular points of $W$ with coordinates in
the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at infinity. For $\sigma$
in the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ and $P \in W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$, let
$\sigma \cdot P$ be the point obtained by applying $\sigma$ to the coordinates of $P$ (the point
at infinity is fixed). Then $1 \cdot P = P$ for every $P \in W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$, where
$1$ is the identity of $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$.

articles.title: The Galois action preserves $p$-torsion points
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over
$\mathbb{Q}$, let $p$ be a natural number, let $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be the group of
nonsingular points of $W$ with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$,
together with the point at infinity, and let $W[p]$ be its subgroup of points $P$ with $pP = 0$.
For $\sigma$ in the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ and $P \in W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$,
let $\sigma \cdot P$ be the point obtained by applying $\sigma$ to the coordinates of $P$ (the
point at infinity is fixed). Then for every $\sigma \in G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ and every $x \in W[p]$,
the point $\sigma \cdot x$ lies in $W[p]$.

articles.title: Galois action on the points of a Weierstrass curve
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over
$\mathbb{Q}$ and let $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be the group of nonsingular points of $W$ with
coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at
infinity. For $\sigma$ in the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$, this is the homomorphism
of additive groups $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) \to W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ that sends the point
$(x, y)$ to $(\sigma(x), \sigma(y))$ and fixes the point at infinity.

For each natural number $p$, restricting this action to the $p$-torsion points gives the mod-$p$
Galois representation.

articles.title: The mod-$p$ Galois representation
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over $\mathbb{Q}$, let
$p$ be a natural number, let $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be the group of nonsingular points of $W$
with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at
infinity, and let $W[p]$ be its subgroup of points $P$ with $pP = 0$, viewed as a
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-module. The mod-$p$ Galois representation is the group homomorphism
from the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ to the group of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-linear
automorphisms of $W[p]$ that sends $\sigma$ to the map $(x, y) \mapsto (\sigma(x), \sigma(y))$,
which fixes the point at infinity.

When $W$ is an elliptic curve $E$, this is the representation usually written $\rho_{E,p}$.

articles.title: Galois automorphisms compose as algebra maps
articles.statement:
Let $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ be the algebraic
closure of $\mathbb{Q}$. For all $\sigma, \tau$ in the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of
$\mathbb{Q}$, the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra homomorphism
$\overline{\mathbb{Q}} \to \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ underlying the product $\sigma\tau$ is the
composite $\sigma \circ \tau$ of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra homomorphisms underlying $\sigma$
and $\tau$.

articles.title: Galois action on $p$-torsion points
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over $\mathbb{Q}$,
let $p$ be a natural number, let $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be the group of nonsingular points of
$W$ with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at
infinity, and let $W[p]$ be its subgroup of points $P$ with $pP = 0$. For $\sigma$ in the
absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$, this is the homomorphism of additive groups
$W[p] \to W[p]$ that sends the point $(x, y)$ to $(\sigma(x), \sigma(y))$ and fixes the point at
infinity.

articles.title: Membership in the $p$-torsion subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over $\mathbb{Q}$,
let $p$ be a natural number, let $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be the group of nonsingular points of
$W$ with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at
infinity, and let $W[p]$ be its $p$-torsion subgroup. A point $x \in W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$
lies in $W[p]$ if and only if $p x = 0$, where $p x$ is the sum of $p$ copies of $x$ and $0$ is
the point at infinity.

articles.title: The $p$-torsion subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $p$ be a
natural number, and let $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be the group of nonsingular points of $W$ with
coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at infinity.
The $p$-torsion subgroup $W[p]$ is the subgroup of points $P \in W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ with
$pP = 0$.

When $W$ is an elliptic curve $E$, this is the group usually written $E[p]$.

articles.title: Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion, easy direction
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring
with fraction field $k$, and let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $k$ given by a Weierstrass
equation with good reduction at $R$. Let $n$ be a natural number whose image in the residue
field of $R$ is nonzero, let $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be a separable closure of $k$, and let
$\mathcal{O}$ be a valuation subring of $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ whose intersection with $k$ is $R$.
Then every element $\sigma$ of the inertia subgroup of $\mathcal{O}$ in
$\mathrm{Gal}(k^{\mathrm{sep}}/k)$ fixes every point $P \in E(k^{\mathrm{sep}})$ with $nP = 0$.

Proof: We use Silverman's elementary valuation filtration at the origin in $(z, w)$ coordinates,
together with reduction to the nonsingular residue curve; see *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*,
IV.1, VII.3, and VII.7.

## Sources

- J. H. Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, 2nd ed., GTM 106, Springer, Theorem VII.7.1.

articles.title: Integer sequences with constant second difference two
articles.statement:
Let $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$
satisfy $d(n-1) + d(n+1) = 2d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and let $q, N$ be integers with
$d(0) = q$ and $d(-1) = N$. Then $d(n) = n^2 + (q + 1 - N)n + q$ for every integer $n$.

articles.title: Hasse bound from Manin degree data
articles.statement:
Let $q$ and $N$ be natural numbers. If there is
Manin degree data for $q$ and $N$, then $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$, computed in the integers.

articles.title: Hasse bound for the odd-characteristic normal form
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$
elements and let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve $y^2 = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_4 x + a_6$ over $F$ (that
is, $a_1 = a_3 = 0$) with nonzero discriminant. If $N$ is the number of points of $W$ over $F$,
including the point at infinity, then $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$.

articles.title: Hasse bound for the supersingular characteristic-two normal form
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite
field of characteristic $2$ with $q$ elements and let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve
$y^2 + a_3 y = x^3 + a_4 x + a_6$ over $F$ (that is, $a_1 = a_2 = 0$) with nonzero discriminant.
If $N$ is the number of points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity, then
$(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$.

articles.title: Hasse bound for the ordinary characteristic-two normal form
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field of
characteristic $2$ with $q$ elements and let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve
$y^2 + xy = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_6$ over $F$ (that is, $a_1 = 1$ and $a_3 = a_4 = 0$) with nonzero
discriminant. If $N$ is the number of points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity,
then $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$.

articles.title: Hasse bound for the characteristic-two normal forms
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field of
characteristic $2$ with $q$ elements and let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over $F$ with nonzero
discriminant that is in one of the two characteristic-two normal forms
$y^2 + xy = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_6$ (that is, $a_1 = 1$ and $a_3 = a_4 = 0$) or
$y^2 + a_3 y = x^3 + a_4 x + a_6$ (that is, $a_1 = a_2 = 0$). If $N$ is the number of points of
$W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity, then $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$.

articles.title: Hasse bound
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and let $E$ be an elliptic curve over
$F$ given by a Weierstrass equation. If $N$ is the number of points of $E$ with coordinates in $F$,
including the point at infinity, then $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$ in $\mathbb{Z}$.

Proof: Manin's elementary polynomial-degree argument on a twist over the rational function field
$F(t)$, done separately for the odd-characteristic and characteristic-two normal forms. In
characteristic two the point count uses the fibres of the additive maps $y \mapsto y^2 + by$ with
$b \in F$, followed by the same projective neighboring-degree recurrence, as in
Chahal--Soomro--Top, *Rocky Mountain J. Math.* 44 (2014).

## Sources

- H. Hasse, J. Reine Angew. Math. 1936; modern Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, 2nd ed.; Lean states integral squared form of |N-(q+1)| ≤ 2√q including point at infinity.

articles.title: Manin degree data over the field with four elements
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field with exactly
four elements, let $W$ be any Weierstrass curve over $F$, and let $N$ be the number of
nonsingular points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity. Then there is Manin degree
data for $(4, N)$: a function $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $d(0) = 4$, $d(-1) = N$,
$d(n - 1) + d(n + 1) = 2 d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and no integer $n$ with
$d(n) = d(n + 1) = 0$.

The proof needs only the elementary bound $N \le 2 \cdot 4 + 1$.

articles.title: Manin degree data over the field with three elements
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field with exactly
three elements, let $W$ be any Weierstrass curve over $F$, and let $N$ be the number of
nonsingular points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity. Then there is Manin degree
data for $(3, N)$: a function $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $d(0) = 3$, $d(-1) = N$,
$d(n - 1) + d(n + 1) = 2 d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and no integer $n$ with
$d(n) = d(n + 1) = 0$.

The proof needs only the elementary bound $N \le 2 \cdot 3 + 1$.

articles.title: Manin degree data over the field with two elements
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field with exactly
two elements, let $W$ be any Weierstrass curve over $F$, and let $N$ be the number of
nonsingular points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity. Then there is Manin degree
data for $(2, N)$: a function $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $d(0) = 2$, $d(-1) = N$,
$d(n - 1) + d(n + 1) = 2 d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and no integer $n$ with
$d(n) = d(n + 1) = 0$.

The proof needs only the elementary bound $N \le 2 \cdot 2 + 1$.

articles.title: Manin degree data for the odd-characteristic normal form
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with
$q$ elements, let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve $y^2 = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_4 x + a_6$ over $F$ (that
is, $a_1 = a_3 = 0$) with nonzero discriminant, and let $N$ be the number of points of $W$ over
$F$, including the point at infinity. Then there is Manin degree data for $(q, N)$: a function
$d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $d(0) = q$, $d(-1) = N$,
$d(n - 1) + d(n + 1) = 2 d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and no integer $n$ with
$d(n) = d(n + 1) = 0$.

articles.title: Manin degree data for the characteristic-two normal forms
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field of
characteristic $2$ with $q$ elements, let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over $F$ with nonzero
discriminant that is in one of the two characteristic-two normal forms
$y^2 + xy = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_6$ (that is, $a_1 = 1$ and $a_3 = a_4 = 0$) or
$y^2 + a_3 y = x^3 + a_4 x + a_6$ (that is, $a_1 = a_2 = 0$), and let $N$ be the number of
points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity. Then there is Manin degree data for
$(q, N)$: a function $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $d(0) = q$, $d(-1) = N$,
$d(n - 1) + d(n + 1) = 2 d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and no integer $n$ with
$d(n) = d(n + 1) = 0$.

articles.title: Manin degree data
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $q$ and $N$, Manin degree data for $q$ and $N$ is
a sequence $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $d(0) = q$, $d(-1) = N$,
$d(n-1) + d(n+1) = 2d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and there is no integer $n$ with
$d(n) = d(n+1) = 0$.

These are the properties of the polynomial-degree sequence used in Manin's proof of the Hasse
bound.

articles.title: Manin degree data from a quadratic
articles.statement:
Let $q$ and $N$ be natural numbers and put
$a = q + 1 - N \in \mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $n^2 + an + q \ge 0$ for every integer $n$, and there is
no integer $n$ at which both $n^2 + an + q$ and $(n+1)^2 + a(n+1) + q$ vanish. Then the sequence
$d(n) = n^2 + an + q$ is Manin degree data for $q$ and $N$.

articles.title: Polynomials with no common irreducible factor form a primitive triple
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a
field and let $a, b, c \in K[X]$ with $c \neq 0$. If no irreducible polynomial in $K[X]$
divides all of $a$, $b$ and $c$, then $a, b, c$ form a primitive triple: there are
$u, v, w \in K[X]$ with $ua + vb + wc = 1$.

articles.title: Primitive triple of polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field. Polynomials $a, b, c \in K[X]$
form a primitive triple when they generate the unit ideal of $K[X]$, that is, when there are
$u, v, w \in K[X]$ with $ua + vb + wc = 1$.

articles.title: Numerator degrees from a primitive presentation of product and sum
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field,
let $u, v, h \in K[X]$ form a primitive triple with $h \neq 0$, and let $x, y \in K(X)$ be
nonzero rational functions with $u/h = xy$ and $v/h = x + y$ in $K(X)$. Then
$\deg u = \deg \operatorname{num}(x) + \deg \operatorname{num}(y)$, where $\operatorname{num}$
denotes the numerator of a rational function written in lowest terms.

articles.title: Discriminant bound for a nonnegative integral quadratic without adjacent zeros
articles.statement:
Let
$a, q \in \mathbb{Z}$. If $n^2 + an + q \ge 0$ for every integer $n$ and there is no integer $n$
with $n^2 + an + q = 0$ and $(n+1)^2 + a(n+1) + q = 0$, then $a^2 \le 4q$.

articles.title: Symmetry of adjacency in a multigraph
articles.statement:
In a multigraph $G$, a vertex $v$ is adjacent to a
vertex $w$ if and only if $w$ is adjacent to $v$.

articles.title: Adjacency in a multigraph
articles.statement:
Two vertices $v$ and $w$ of a multigraph $G$ are adjacent when
the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive.

articles.title: Reversing an ascending edge gives a descending edge
articles.statement:
In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano, for
vertices $v$ and $w$, $(v, w)$ is an ascending edge if and only if $(w, v)$ is a descending
edge.

articles.title: Every vertex is connected to itself
articles.statement:
In a multigraph $G$, every vertex $v$ is connected to
$v$.

articles.title: Connectivity of vertices in a multigraph
articles.statement:
Two vertices $v$ and $w$ of a multigraph $G$ are
connected when they are related by the reflexive-transitive closure of adjacency, that is, when
there is a finite sequence of vertices $v = u_0, u_1, \dots, u_k = w$ with $k \ge 0$ and $u_i$
adjacent to $u_{i+1}$ for each $i < k$.

articles.title: Degree splits over a predicate and its complement
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph on a finite
vertex set $V$, let $v \in V$ and let $P$ be a decidable predicate on $V$. Then the degree of $v$
equals the degree of $v$ restricted to $P$ plus the degree of $v$ restricted to $\neg P$.

articles.title: Restricted degree depends only on the neighbours
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph on a finite
vertex set $V$, let $v \in V$ and let $P$ and $Q$ be decidable predicates on $V$. If
$P(w) \iff Q(w)$ for every vertex $w$ whose edge multiplicity with $v$ is positive, then the
degree of $v$ restricted to $P$ equals the degree of $v$ restricted to $Q$.

articles.title: Degree restricted to a predicate
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph on a finite vertex set $V$ with
edge multiplicity $m$, let $v \in V$ and let $P$ be a decidable predicate on $V$. The degree of
$v$ restricted to $P$ is $\sum_{w \in V,\, P(w)} m(v, w)$.

articles.title: Degree of a vertex in a multigraph
articles.statement:
For a multigraph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ with edge
multiplicity $m$, the degree of a vertex $v$ is $\sum_{w \in V} m(v, w)$. A loop at $v$
contributes its multiplicity once, matching the outgoing-isogeny convention.

articles.title: Reversing a descending edge gives an ascending edge
articles.statement:
In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano, for
vertices $v$ and $w$, $(v, w)$ is a descending edge if and only if $(w, v)$ is an ascending
edge.

articles.title: Every edge of an isogeny volcano is horizontal, descending or ascending
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be an $\ell$-isogeny volcano, with levels numbered from $0$ at the surface, and let $v, w$
be vertices of $C$ whose edge multiplicity is positive. Then $(v, w)$ is a horizontal edge (both
$v$ and $w$ have level $0$), a descending edge (the level of $w$ is the level of $v$ plus one) or
an ascending edge (the level of $v$ is the level of $w$ plus one).

articles.title: Ascending edge
articles.statement:
In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is an
ascending edge when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and $w$ lies one level
above $v$, that is, the level of $w$ plus one equals the level of $v$ (level $0$ being the
surface).

articles.title: Connected multigraph
articles.statement:
A multigraph $G$ is connected when every two vertices $v$ and $w$
of $G$ are joined by a walk, that is, $w$ is reachable from $v$ by a finite (possibly empty)
sequence of steps along edges of positive multiplicity.

articles.title: Descending edge
articles.statement:
In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is a
descending edge when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and $w$ lies one level
below $v$, that is, the level of $v$ plus one equals the level of $w$ (level $0$ being the
surface).

articles.title: Floor vertices are those whose level equals the depth
articles.statement:
A vertex $v$ of an
$\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ lies on the floor of $C$ if and only if the level of $v$, as a natural
number, equals the depth of $C$.

articles.title: Floor of a volcano
articles.statement:
A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ of depth $d$ lies on
the floor of $C$ when its level is $d$, the last of the levels $0, 1, \dots, d$.

articles.title: Horizontal edge
articles.statement:
In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is a
horizontal edge when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and both $v$ and $w$
lie on the surface, that is, both have level $0$.

articles.title: Surface vertices are those of level zero
articles.statement:
A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$
lies on the surface of $C$ if and only if the level of $v$, as a natural number, is $0$.

articles.title: Surface of a volcano
articles.statement:
A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ lies on the surface
of $C$ when its level is $0$.

articles.title: Vertical edge
articles.statement:
In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is a
vertical edge when it is a descending edge or an ascending edge, that is, when the edge
multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and the levels of $v$ and $w$ differ by exactly
one.

articles.title: Isogeny volcano
articles.statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime. An $\ell$-isogeny volcano consists of a finite
vertex set $V$, a multigraph on $V$ with edge multiplicities $m(v, w)$, a depth $d \in \mathbb{N}$,
a surjective level map $\mathrm{lev} : V \to \{0, 1, \dots, d\}$ and a surface degree
$s \in \mathbb{N}$ with $s \le 2$, subject to the following conditions, where the surface is the
set of vertices of level $0$. Every surface vertex $v$ satisfies
$\sum_{w \in V,\ \mathrm{lev}(w) = 0} m(v, w) = s$. Every vertex $v$ of positive level has a
unique parent: $\sum_{w \in V,\ \mathrm{lev}(w) + 1 = \mathrm{lev}(v)} m(v, w) = 1$. Whenever
$m(v, w) > 0$, either $v$ and $w$ both lie on the surface or their levels differ by exactly one.
Every vertex $v$ with $\mathrm{lev}(v) < d$ has degree $\sum_{w \in V} m(v, w) = \ell + 1$, where a
loop at $v$ contributes its multiplicity once. Finally, the multigraph is connected: any two
vertices are joined by a path along which consecutive vertices have positive edge multiplicity.

articles.title: Multigraph
articles.statement:
A multigraph on a vertex set $V$ is given by an edge multiplicity function $m$
that assigns to every two vertices $v, w \in V$ a natural number $m(v, w)$ and is symmetric:
$m(v, w) = m(w, v)$ for all $v, w \in V$. Loops are permitted: $m(v, v)$ may be positive.

articles.title: Surface regularity of an isogeny volcano
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be an $\ell$-isogeny volcano with edge
multiplicities $m$ and surface degree $s$. For every surface vertex $v$ of $C$, that is, every
vertex of level $0$, the sum of $m(v, w)$ over all surface vertices $w$ of $C$ equals $s$.

This restates the surface-regularity condition of an isogeny volcano in terms of the surface
predicate.

articles.title: Depth of an isogeny volcano
articles.statement:
The depth of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ is the natural
number $d$ recorded in $C$: the levels of the vertices of $C$ are exactly $0, 1, \dots, d$, with
level $0$ the surface and level $d$ the floor.

articles.title: Elliptic curves with point count divisible by 4 and Ramanujan graphs on two vertices
articles.statement:
Let
$p$ be an odd prime, let $a \in \{1, 2\}$, and let $F$ be a finite field with $q = p^a$ elements. A
natural number $N$ is the number $\#E(F)$ of $F$-points (counting the point at infinity) of some
elliptic curve $E$ over $F$ with $4 \mid N$ if and only if there are natural numbers $l$ and $m$
with $N = 2m$, $2l + m = q + 1$, $m > 0$ and $(2l - m)^2 \le 4q$.

In graph terms, $X(l, m)$ is the two-vertex graph with $l$ loops at each vertex and $m$ edges
between the two vertices. For such $l$ and $m$ it is $(q + 1)$-regular, it is connected exactly
when $m > 0$, and its non-trivial eigenvalue is $2l - m$, so the last condition says that $X(l, m)$
is Ramanujan. The paper states a bijection from $F$-isogeny classes of such curves to these
graphs; the statement above is its point-count form, and injectivity on isogeny classes is Tate's
theorem.

## Sources

- Daniel Vallières, *Elliptic Curves over Finite Fields and Ramanujan Graphs on Two Vertices*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A8, Theorem 8.

articles.title: Waterhouse's theorem on Frobenius traces
Ordinary elliptic curves with point count divisible by 4 and Ramanujan graphs on two vertices
articles.statement:
**Ordinary elliptic curves with point count divisible by 4 and Ramanujan graphs on two
vertices.** Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $a \ge 1$, and let $F$ be a finite field with $q = p^a$
elements. A natural number $N$ is the number $\#E(F)$ of $F$-points (counting the point at
infinity) of some elliptic curve $E$ over $F$ with $4 \mid N$ whose Frobenius trace
$q + 1 - \#E(F)$ is coprime to $p$ if and only if there are natural numbers $l$ and $m$ with
$N = 2m$, $2l + m = q + 1$, $m > 0$, $(2l - m)^2 \le 4q$ and $2m \not\equiv 1 \pmod p$.

A Frobenius trace coprime to $p$ is the paper's criterion for $E$ to be ordinary; since $p \mid q$,
the trace $q + 1 - 2m$ is coprime to $p$ exactly when $2m \not\equiv 1 \pmod p$. In graph terms,
$X(l, m)$ is the two-vertex graph with $l$ loops at each vertex and $m$ edges between the two
vertices; it is $(q + 1)$-regular, connected exactly when $m > 0$, and Ramanujan exactly when
$(2l - m)^2 \le 4q$. The paper states a bijection from $F$-isogeny classes of such curves to these
graphs; the statement above is its point-count form, and injectivity on isogeny classes is Tate's
theorem.

## Sources

- Daniel Vallières, *Elliptic Curves over Finite Fields and Ramanujan Graphs on Two Vertices*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A8, Theorem 9.

articles.title: Frobenius trace
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a finite field $F$ with $q$ elements,
and let $\#W(F)$ be the number of nonsingular $F$-points of $W$, counting the point at infinity.
The Frobenius trace of $W$ is the integer $a_q(W) = q + 1 - \#W(F)$.

articles.title: Ramanujan graphs give Weil numbers
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a natural number and let $A$ be a symmetric
$n \times n$ matrix with integer entries such that every complex root $\mu \ne q + 1$ of its
characteristic polynomial satisfies $|\mu| \le 2\sqrt{q}$. Let $\mu \ne q + 1$ be a complex root
of the characteristic polynomial of $A$ and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy
$\alpha^2 - \mu\alpha + q = 0$. Then $\alpha$ is an algebraic integer, and every complex root of
the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ has absolute value $\sqrt{q}$; that is,
$\alpha$ is a Weil $q$-number.

When $A$ is the adjacency matrix of a $(q + 1)$-regular graph $X$, the hypothesis says that $X$ is
Ramanujan, and the numbers $\alpha$ are the inverse roots of
$P_X(u) = \prod_{\mu \ne q + 1} (1 - \mu u + q u^2)$. The paper takes $q = p^a$ and $X$
connected; neither assumption is needed.

## Sources

- Daniel Vallières, *Elliptic Curves over Finite Fields and Ramanujan Graphs on Two Vertices*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A8, Proposition 1.

articles.title: Point count plus Frobenius trace
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a finite field $F$
with $q$ elements, and let $\#W(F)$ be the number of nonsingular $F$-points of $W$, counting the
point at infinity. Then $\#W(F) + a_q(W) = q + 1$, where $a_q(W)$ is the Frobenius trace of $W$.

articles.title: Point count from the Frobenius trace
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a finite field
$F$ with $q$ elements, and let $\#W(F)$ be the number of nonsingular $F$-points of $W$, counting
the point at infinity. Then $\#W(F) = q + 1 - a_q(W)$, where $a_q(W)$ is the Frobenius trace of
$W$.

articles.title: Point count from affine solutions
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be an elliptic curve in Weierstrass form over a
finite field $F$. The number of $F$-points of $W$, counting the point at infinity, is one more than
the number of pairs $(x, y) \in F \times F$ satisfying the Weierstrass equation of $W$.

articles.title: Upper bound on the point count
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a finite field $F$
with $q$ elements. The number of nonsingular $F$-points of $W$, counting the point at infinity, is
at most $2q + 1$.

Each $x \in F$ lies under at most two affine points, since the Weierstrass equation is quadratic
in $y$.

articles.title: Ihara's criterion for Ramanujan graphs
articles.statement:
Let $q \ge 2$ be a natural number and let $A$ be a
symmetric $n \times n$ matrix with integer entries. Every complex root $\mu \ne q + 1$ of the
characteristic polynomial of $A$ satisfies $|\mu| \le 2\sqrt{q}$ if and only if, for every such
root $\mu \ne q + 1$, every complex number $s$ with $1 - \mu q^{-s} + q^{1 - 2s} = 0$ has real
part $1/2$.

When $A$ is the adjacency matrix of a $(q + 1)$-regular graph $X$, the left side says that $X$ is
Ramanujan. Writing $\zeta_X$ for the Ihara zeta function of $X$, the numbers $s$ on the right are
the non-trivial zeros of $Q_X(s) = \zeta_X(q^{-s})^{-1}$, that is, the zeros of
$P_X(q^{-s}) = \prod_{\mu \ne q + 1} (1 - \mu q^{-s} + q^{1 - 2s})$. The roots $\mu$ are real
because $A$ is symmetric. The paper also assumes that $X$ is connected and regular and has at
least two vertices; these assumptions are not needed, since the equivalence holds root by root.

## Sources

- Daniel Vallières, *Elliptic Curves over Finite Fields and Ramanujan Graphs on Two Vertices*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A8, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Supersingular elliptic curves
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $E$ be an elliptic curve over an
algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Then $E$ is called
supersingular when every point $P \in E(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ with $pP = 0$ is $P = 0$.

## Sources

- arXiv:2308.11539v1, `main.tex`, lines 164–170, which gives the equivalent condition that for every positive integer $r$, every point $P$ with $p^r P = 0$ is $P = 0$; this definition is its case $r = 1$.

articles.title: Supersingularity from trivial prime-power torsion
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $E$ be an
elliptic curve over an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. If
for every integer $r \ge 1$ the only point $P \in E(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ with $p^r P = 0$ is
$P = 0$, then $E$ is supersingular.

articles.title: Supersingular curves have trivial prime-power torsion
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $E$ be a
supersingular elliptic curve over an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ of
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Then for every integer $r \ge 1$, every point
$P \in E(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ with $p^r P = 0$ is $P = 0$.

articles.title: Variable changes act bijectively on affine coordinates
articles.statement:
For a variable change
$C = (u, r, s, t)$ over a field $F$, the map $(x, y) \mapsto (u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$
is a bijection $F^2 \to F^2$, whose inverse is the corresponding map of the inverse variable
change $C^{-1}$.

articles.title: Variable changes biject affine solutions
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a field $F$,
let $C = (u, r, s, t)$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed curve. The map
$(x, y) \mapsto (u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$ is a bijection from the solutions
$(x, y) \in F^2$ of the Weierstrass equation of $C \cdot W$ onto the solutions in $F^2$ of the
Weierstrass equation of $W$; its inverse is the corresponding map of $C^{-1}$.

articles.title: Variable changes transform the Weierstrass equation
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over
a field $F$, let $C = (u, r, s, t)$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed
curve. A pair $(x, y) \in F^2$ satisfies the Weierstrass equation of $C \cdot W$ if and only if
$(u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$ satisfies the Weierstrass equation of $W$.

articles.title: Coordinate map of a Weierstrass variable change
articles.statement:
For a variable change $C = (u, r, s, t)$
over a field $F$, with $u \in F^\times$ and $r, s, t \in F$, the affine coordinate map of $C$
sends $(x, y) \in F^2$ to $(u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$.

articles.title: Variable changes preserve the point count
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be an elliptic Weierstrass curve over
a finite field $F$, let $C$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed curve.
Then $C \cdot W$ and $W$ have the same number of rational points.

articles.title: Variable changes biject rational points
articles.statement:
Let $W$ be an elliptic Weierstrass curve over a
field $F$, let $C = (u, r, s, t)$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed
curve. There is a bijection from the rational points of $C \cdot W$ to the rational points of
$W$, where in both cases the point at infinity is included; it sends the point at infinity to
the point at infinity and an affine point $(x, y)$ to $(u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$.

articles.title: The ideal of a point on a Weierstrass curve is nonzero
articles.statement: The ideal generated by `X - x` and `Y - y` is nonzero.

articles.title: Reduced closed immersions with equal range are isomorphic
articles.statement:
Two reduced closed immersions with the same range are isomorphic over
the target.

articles.title: Closed immersions of constant fibre rank are isomorphisms
articles.statement:
A closed immersion between maps of constant fibre rank is an
isomorphism.

articles.title: Closed immersions flat over the base of an étale map are open
articles.statement:
A closed immersion whose composite with an étale map is flat and
locally of finite presentation is open.

articles.title: Surjectivity is stable under base change
articles.statement: Surjectivity transfers along pullback squares.

articles.title: Universal closedness descends along surjective closed immersions
articles.statement:
Universal closedness transfers along a pullback square whose base map is
a surjective closed immersion.

articles.title: Separatedness descends along surjective closed immersions
articles.statement:
Separatedness transfers along a pullback square whose base map is a
surjective closed immersion.

articles.title: Properness descends along surjective closed immersions
articles.statement:
Properness transfers along a pullback square whose base map is a
surjective closed immersion.

articles.title: Closed immersions are stable under base change
articles.statement: Closed immersions transfer along pullback squares.

articles.title: Geometrically irreducible morphisms are geometrically connected
articles.statement: A geometrically irreducible morphism is geometrically connected.

articles.title: Geometric irreducibility over an algebraically closed field
articles.statement:
An irreducible scheme over an algebraically closed field is geometrically
irreducible.

articles.title: Integral schemes over algebraically closed fields: geometric integrality
articles.statement: An integral scheme over an algebraically closed field is geometrically integral.

articles.title: Reduced schemes over a perfect field are geometrically reduced
articles.statement:
A reduced scheme over a perfect field is
geometrically reduced.

articles.title: Density of rational points over an algebraically closed field
articles.statement: Rational points over an algebraically closed field are dense.

articles.title: Pullback points determined by projections given a residue isomorphism
articles.statement:
Two points of a pullback with the same first and second projections are
equal, when the residue field map at the second point's first projection is
an isomorphism.

articles.title: Surjective morphisms of finite type lift rational points
articles.statement:
A surjective morphism locally of finite type lifts rational points over
an algebraically closed field.

articles.title: Closed points of finite-type schemes over algebraically closed fields
articles.statement:
A closed point of a scheme of finite type over an algebraically
closed field lifts to a point over the base.

articles.title: Valuative criterion for factoring sections through an open subscheme
articles.statement:
A section over a valuation ring factors through a universally closed
open subscheme exactly when the generic point does.

articles.title: Morphisms are determined by their values on rational points
articles.statement:
Two morphisms over an algebraically closed field agreeing on all
rational points are equal.

articles.title: Universal property of the reduced subscheme on a closed subset
articles.statement:
A map from a reduced scheme landing in a closed subset lifts uniquely
to the subscheme cut out by the vanishing ideal.

articles.title: Unique lifting of maps from reduced schemes through closed immersions
articles.statement:
A map from a reduced scheme into a closed immersion whose range
contains the image lifts uniquely.

articles.title: Reducedness and kernel bound for the vanishing-ideal subscheme
articles.statement:
The subscheme cut out by a vanishing ideal is reduced, and its ideal
sheaf is contained in the kernel of any map from a reduced scheme landing
in the subset.

articles.title: The subscheme cut out by a vanishing ideal is reduced
articles.statement: The subscheme cut out by a vanishing ideal is reduced.

articles.title: Vanishing ideal lies in the kernel of maps from reduced schemes
articles.statement:
The vanishing ideal of a closed subset is contained in the kernel of
any map from a reduced scheme landing in the subset.

articles.title: Smooth maps from a preconnected scheme have constant relative dimension
articles.statement:
A smooth morphism from a preconnected scheme is smooth of some fixed
relative dimension.

articles.title: Smooth morphisms preserve reducedness
articles.statement: A smooth morphism with reduced locally Noetherian target has reduced source.

articles.title: Smooth schemes over a field are reduced
articles.statement: A scheme smooth over a field is reduced.

articles.title: Krull dimension does not increase along faithfully flat maps
articles.statement: Krull dimension does not increase along faithfully flat ring maps.

articles.title: Krull dimension of a standard smooth algebra
articles.statement:
A standard smooth algebra of relative dimension `n` has Krull dimension
at most `n`.

articles.title: Krull dimension of a standard smooth algebra over a field
articles.statement:
A standard smooth algebra map from a field has Krull dimension at most
the relative dimension.

articles.title: Dimension of a scheme smooth of relative dimension $n$
articles.statement:
A scheme smooth of relative dimension `n` over a field has topological
Krull dimension at most `n`.

articles.title: Characterization of varieties
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme with a
structure morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$. Then $X$ is a variety over $k$ if and only if
this structure morphism is separated, locally of finite type, quasi-compact and geometrically
reduced.

articles.title: Geometrically reduced variety over a field
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A scheme $X$ with a
chosen structure morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$ is a *variety* over $k$ if this morphism
is separated, of finite type (quasi-compact and locally of finite type), and geometrically
reduced.

articles.title: Varieties are quasi-separated
articles.statement:
If $X$ is a variety over a field $k$, then its structure
morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$ is quasi-separated, since it is separated.

articles.title: Affine coordinates of a projective point
articles.statement:
For a field $K$ and a point
$p \in \mathbb{P}^n(K)$, let $v = (v_0, \dots, v_n) \in K^{n+1} \setminus \{0\}$ be the chosen
representative of $p$ and $i$ its chart index (a chosen index with $v_i \neq 0$). The affine cone
coordinates of $p$ are the vector $q \in K^{n+1}$ with $q_j = v_j / v_i$ for every $j$; in
particular $q_i = 1$.

articles.title: Bézout's theorem (with multiplicity)
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field, let
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $f_1, \dots, f_n \in K[X_0, \dots, X_n]$ and integers
$d_1, \dots, d_n \ge 1$ be such that each $f_k$ is homogeneous of degree $d_k$ and has total
degree exactly $d_k$. Suppose the common projective zero set
$Z = V(f_1) \cap \dots \cap V(f_n) \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n(K)$ is finite. Then
$\sum_{p \in Z} i_p(f_1, \dots, f_n) = d_1 d_2 \cdots d_n$ in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$,
where $i_p(f_1, \dots, f_n)$ is the intersection multiplicity of $f_1, \dots, f_n$ at $p$.

The total degree hypothesis rules out $f_k = 0$, which is homogeneous of every degree but has
total degree $0$.

## Sources

- É. Bézout, *Théorie générale des équations algébriques*, Paris, 1779. Modern projective formulation: see Eisenbud, *Commutative Algebra*, Chapter 12, or Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, Ch. I §7. Listed as §50 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `bezout_projective_multiplicity` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Chart index of a projective point
articles.statement:
For a field $K$ and a point $p \in \mathbb{P}^n(K)$
with chosen representative $v = (v_0, \dots, v_n) \in K^{n+1} \setminus \{0\}$, the chart index of
$p$ is a fixed choice of an index $i \in \{0, \dots, n\}$ with $v_i \neq 0$.

articles.title: Evaluation at an affine point
articles.statement:
For a field $K$ and a point
$q = (q_0, \dots, q_n) \in K^{n+1}$, this is the ring homomorphism $K[X_0, \dots, X_n] \to K$
sending each polynomial $g$ to its value $g(q)$; it fixes $K$ and sends $X_j$ to $q_j$.

articles.title: Intersection multiplicity at a projective point
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and
$f_1, \dots, f_n \in K[X_0, \dots, X_n]$. For a point $p \in \mathbb{P}^n(K)$, let $i$ be its chart
index, $q \in K^{n+1}$ its affine cone coordinates (so $q_i = 1$), and $\mathcal{O}_q$ the
localization of $K[X_0, \dots, X_n]$ at the maximal ideal of $q$. The intersection multiplicity
of $f_1, \dots, f_n$ at $p$ is the length, as an $\mathcal{O}_q$-module, of the quotient of
$\mathcal{O}_q$ by the ideal generated by $f_1, \dots, f_n$ and $X_i - 1$; it is an element of
$\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.

The value is $\infty$ exactly when this quotient does not have finite length, for example along
a positive-dimensional component of the common zero set.

articles.title: Local ring of affine space at a point
articles.statement:
For a field $K$ and a point $q \in K^{n+1}$, this is
the localization of $K[X_0, \dots, X_n]$ at the maximal ideal of $q$ (the ideal of polynomials
vanishing at $q$), that is, the local ring of affine space $\mathbb{A}^{n+1}$ at $q$.

articles.title: Maximal ideal of an affine point
articles.statement:
For a field $K$ and a point $q \in K^{n+1}$, this is the
ideal of $K[X_0, \dots, X_n]$ consisting of the polynomials $g$ with $g(q) = 0$, that is, the
kernel of evaluation at $q$.

It is a maximal ideal, since evaluation at $q$ is surjective onto $K$.

articles.title: Projective space
articles.statement:
For a division ring $K$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the projective space
$\mathbb{P}^n(K)$ is the projectivization of $K^{n+1}$: the set of nonzero vectors of $K^{n+1}$
modulo multiplication by nonzero scalars, equivalently the lines through the origin.

articles.title: Projective vanishing set
articles.statement:
For a field $K$ and a polynomial $f \in K[X_0, \dots, X_n]$, the
vanishing set of $f$ is the set of points $p \in \mathbb{P}^n(K)$ such that $f(v) = 0$, where
$v \in K^{n+1} \setminus \{0\}$ is the chosen representative of $p$.

When $f$ is homogeneous of degree $d$, $f(\lambda v) = \lambda^d f(v)$, so this set does not depend
on the choice of representatives.

articles.title: Birational automorphisms over a base
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be an irreducible scheme over a scheme
$S$. The birational automorphisms of $X$ over $S$ form the subgroup of the group of birational
self-maps of $X$ consisting of those birational maps whose forward rational map
$X \dashrightarrow X$ is compatible with the structure maps to $S$.

articles.title: Birational map
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes. A birational map from $X$ to $Y$
consists of dominant rational maps $f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y$ and
$g \colon Y \dashrightarrow X$ that are mutually inverse: $g \circ f$ is the identity rational
map of $X$ and $f \circ g$ is the identity rational map of $Y$.

articles.title: Cremona group
articles.statement:
For a field $k$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Cremona group
$\mathrm{Cr}_n(k)$ is the group of birational automorphisms of affine $n$-space
$\mathbb{A}^n_k$ over $\operatorname{Spec} k$.

articles.title: Cremona group generated by pseudo-regularizable elements
articles.statement:
For a field $k$ and
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the proposition that the Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_n(k)$ is
generated, as a group, by its pseudo-regularizable elements.

articles.title: Birational maps over a base
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes over a scheme $S$.
A birational map from $X$ to $Y$ is over $S$ when its forward rational map
$X \dashrightarrow Y$ is compatible with the structure maps to $S$.

Its inverse rational map is then compatible with the structure maps to $S$ as well.

articles.title: Pseudo-isomorphism
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes. A partial isomorphism from $X$ to $Y$,
that is, an isomorphism $U \cong V$ between dense open subschemes $U \subseteq X$ and
$V \subseteq Y$, is a pseudo-isomorphism if it is an isomorphism in codimension one: every
point of $X$ outside $U$ and every point of $Y$ outside $V$ has coheight at least $2$ in the
specialization order of points.

articles.title: Pseudo-regularizable birational automorphism
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a variety over a field $k$. A
birational automorphism $\varphi$ of $X$ is pseudo-regularizable if there exist a variety $X'$
over $k$, a birational map $\alpha \colon X \dashrightarrow X'$ over $k$, and a partial
isomorphism $\gamma$ from $X'$ to itself over $k$ that is a pseudo-isomorphism (an isomorphism
in codimension one), such that $\varphi = \alpha^{-1} \circ \gamma \circ \alpha$, where $\gamma$
is viewed as a birational map. The variety $X'$ need not be smooth or projective.

## Sources

- H.-Y. Lin and E. Shinder, Motivic invariants of birational maps, Definition 4.1.

articles.title: Pseudo-regularization of a birational automorphism
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a variety over a field
$k$ and let $\varphi$ be a birational automorphism of $X$. A pseudo-regularization of $\varphi$
consists of a variety $X'$ over $k$, a birational map $\alpha \colon X \dashrightarrow X'$ over
$k$, and a partial isomorphism $\gamma$ from $X'$ to itself over $k$ that is a
pseudo-isomorphism, such that $\varphi = \alpha^{-1} \circ \gamma \circ \alpha$, where $\gamma$
is viewed as a birational map.

articles.title: Identity birational map
articles.statement:
For an irreducible scheme $X$, the identity birational map of
$X$ has the identity rational map of $X$ as both its forward and its inverse map.

articles.title: Inverse birational map
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes. The inverse of a
birational map from $X$ to $Y$ is the birational map from $Y$ to $X$ whose forward map is the
inverse rational map of the original and whose inverse map is its forward rational map.

articles.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a number field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements
articles.statement:
Let $k$
be a number field. The Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_3(k)$, the group of birational automorphisms of
affine $3$-space over $k$, is not generated by its pseudo-regularizable elements.

This is Theorem 1.2 (1) (a) of Lin and Shinder.

## Sources

- H.-Y. Lin and E. Shinder, `Motivic invariants of birational maps`, Annals of Math, 199 (1) 2024. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_motivic_invariants` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over a number field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements
articles.statement:
**$\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over a number field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable

function field $F(X)$. The Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_3(F(X))$, the group of birational

articles.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over a finite field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements
articles.statement:
**$\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over a finite field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable

articles.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over an algebraically closed field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements
articles.statement:
**$\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a function field over an algebraically closed field is not generated by

articles.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_n$ of a subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements for $n \ge 4$
articles.statement:
**$\mathrm{Cr}_n$ of a subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ is not generated by pseudo-regularizable
elements for $n \ge 4$.** Let $k$ be a subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ and let $n \ge 4$. The Cremona group

articles.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_n$ of an infinite field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements for $n \ge 5$
articles.statement:
**$\mathrm{Cr}_n$ of an infinite field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements for
$n \ge 5$.** Let $k$ be an infinite field and let $n \ge 5$. The Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_n(k)$,
